# LocalQA: Agent for your agents

![LocalQA: Agent for your agents](./assets/localqa-agent-for-agents.svg)

LocalQA is a Bonsai-backed local sidecar for frontier coding agents.

Your main coding agent should plan, reason, and write code. LocalQA handles the noisy local work around it: logs, browser evidence, repo context, docs, previous work memory, redaction, and context cleanup. It returns compact verified evidence so the frontier model spends less context on raw dumps.

```text
Frontier model = planner and implementer
Bonsai = local worker model
LocalQA = sidecar layer for evidence, memory, and handoff cleanup
```

## What we are launching

LocalQA launches with two surfaces:

| Surface | Role | Who should use it first? |
|---|---|---|
| MCP server | Primary public interface | Anyone using an MCP-compatible coding agent |
| OpenCode plugin | Deeper native integration | OpenCode users who want rules, hooks, vault handles, and automatic compaction |

The short version:

```text
LocalQA is MCP-first, with an OpenCode plugin integration.
```

## Why this exists

Coding agents are powerful, but they waste context on low-value evidence work:

| Noisy input | What LocalQA does locally |
|---|---|
| Long logs and stack traces | Dedupes, ranks root-cause lines, returns compact evidence |
| Browser console/network/DOM dumps | Runs local Playwright QA and summarizes verified issues |
| Repo scans and repeated file reads | Compresses codebase evidence into source/test/risk signals |
| Prior work rediscovery | Writes and queries project-local memory |
| Raw handoff payloads | Redacts and prepares compact payloads before cloud reasoning |
| Tool-output bloat | In OpenCode plugin mode, can compact large tool outputs before they stay in context |

## MCP vs OpenCode plugin

| Dimension | MCP mode | OpenCode plugin mode |
|---|---|---|
| Positioning | Portable default | Advanced native workflow |
| Main interface | MCP server over stdio | OpenCode plugin + native tools |
| Primary tool | `local_agent_run` | `local_agent_run` |
| Extra tool | Hidden in strict mode | `answer_from_handle` for local vault queries |
| Host support | Any MCP-compatible agent | OpenCode only |
| Tool surface | One strict public tool | Native tools plus plugin hooks |
| Enforcement strength | Agent chooses to call MCP | Stronger rules/hooks inside the host |
| Large tool-output compaction | Only when routed through LocalQA | Can happen automatically through plugin hook |
| Long-session memory | Returned as tool output | Rules/compaction can preserve vault/memory reminders |
| First-prompt privacy | No | No full first-prompt firewall |
| Best use case | Broad launch and easy adoption | Power users who want deeper local workflows |

MCP says: the main agent can call LocalQA.

OpenCode plugin says: the agent host knows LocalQA exists and can help keep noisy tool output out of context.

## How the MCP flow works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  U[User gives short task or file/url pointer] --> A[Frontier coding agent]
  A --> M[LocalQA MCP server]
  M --> T[local_agent_run]
  T --> E[Local files, browser, repo, docs, memory]
  E --> B[Bonsai local worker]
  B --> C[Compact verified report]

```

Use MCP when you want the portable one-tool local assistant.

```bash
LOCALQA_PUBLIC_SURFACE=agent-strict npm run localqa:mcp
```

Tell your coding agent:

```text
Use LocalQA as the local evidence and memory layer. Before reading large logs, browser evidence, DOM dumps, screenshots, network traces, or repeated repo context, call local_agent_run. Prefer directed mode for complex work.
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  U[User in OpenCode] --> O[OpenCode host]
  O --> R[LocalQA rules]
  O --> H[Plugin hooks]
  O --> LT[Native tools]
  H --> K[Compact large tool output]
  LT --> L[local_agent_run]
  LT --> Q[answer_from_handle]
  L --> B[Bonsai local worker]
  B --> V[Local vault and memory]
  V --> O
```

Use OpenCode mode when you want deeper integration:

| Feature | What it gives you |

| `.opencode/LOCALQA_RULES.md` | Agent instructions for when to use LocalQA |
| `.opencode/tools/local_agent_run.ts` | Local sidecar agent as a native OpenCode tool |

## Example tasks

Good prompt:

```text
Use LocalQA to analyze ./logs/dev.log and return only verified auth/session errors. Do not paste raw logs into cloud context.
```

Good directed task shape:

```json
{
  "controlMode": "directed",
  "task": "Investigate login QA failures and return verified evidence only.",
  "directedSteps": [
    {
      "tool": "browser_qa",
      "url": "http://localhost:3000/login",
      "task": "Collect screenshot, console, network, accessibility, and form-state evidence."
    },
    {
      "tool": "log_analysis",
      "filePath": "./logs/dev.log",
      "task": "Find auth, session, csrf, 401, 500, and stack-trace evidence."
    }
  ],
  "outputContract": {
    "maxTokens": 1600,
    "include": ["verified_findings", "evidence", "likely_files", "risks", "next_actions"],
    "exclude": ["raw_dom", "full_logs", "screenshot_metadata"]
  }
}
```

Bad prompt:

```text
Here are 50,000 characters of logs pasted directly into cloud chat...
```

If you paste raw data into cloud chat, it already went to the cloud before MCP can help.

## What LocalQA is not

| Not this | Actual boundary |
|---|---|
| A frontier-model replacement | The frontier model still plans and writes code |
| A guarantee that pasted chat data stays local | Pasted cloud-chat text is already sent to the cloud |
| A patch-correctness proof system | Compression benchmarks are not patch correctness benchmarks |
| A formal DLP/security product | Redaction exists, but this is alpha software |
| Browser QA that works identically everywhere | Local browser permissions vary by machine |

# LocalQA Browser MCP

LocalQA is a local-first browser QA and research agent for coding assistants.

It runs beside the coding agent as an MCP server. The browser work happens locally through Playwright. For the initial release, local model triage is standardized on `Bonsai-8B.gguf` served through the native Prism/llama.cpp `llama-server` OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

The goal is to keep the main LLM focused on coding decisions while LocalQA handles repetitive browser work: UI testing, bug reproduction, page extraction, docs research, source comparison, screenshots, DOM summaries, console/network evidence, and compact report handoff.

The public product direction is documented in [`../docs/LOCAL_AGENT_MCP_PROJECT_SPEC.md`](../docs/LOCAL_AGENT_MCP_PROJECT_SPEC.md).

Client setup examples are in [`../docs/LOCAL_AGENT_MCP_CLIENT_SETUP.md`](../docs/LOCAL_AGENT_MCP_CLIENT_SETUP.md).

Release checklist is in [`../docs/LOCAL_AGENT_MCP_RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md`](../docs/LOCAL_AGENT_MCP_RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md).

## Public one-call facade

Use `local_agent_run` first. It is the local sub-agent manager tool for coding agents.

Example:

```json
{
  "tool": "local_agent_run",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "http://localhost:3000/login",
    "task": "Test login and sign-up UX. Report only verified issues.",
    "contextBudgetTokens": 6000,
    "llmProvider": "openai-compatible",
    "llmModel": "Bonsai-8B.gguf",
    "llmEndpoint": "http://127.0.0.1:18081/v1/chat/completions",
    "llmTemperature": 0.5,
    "llmTopK": 20,
    "llmTopP": 0.85
  }
}
```

Supported high-level modes:

| Mode | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `browser_qa` | Test one page with Playwright, deterministic evidence, screenshots, and optional local LLM triage |
| `site_qa` | Discover or accept multiple routes and aggregate QA results |
| `research` | Extract and summarize coding-related web sources |
| `extract_page` | Convert one page into compact structured context |
| `log_analysis` | Deduplicate and rank long logs before the main LLM sees them |
| `prompt_cleanup` | Compress large prompt dumps into a budgeted high-signal packet |
| `context_cleanup` | Generic local context cleaning for raw evidence dumps |
| `handoff_gate` | Prepare local-first compact payload before sending evidence to a main LLM or external server |

The lower-level MCP tools remain available for advanced workflows and debugging.

Release default is `LOCALQA_PUBLIC_SURFACE=agent-strict`, so the main agent sees only `local_agent_run` unless you explicitly override to `agent` or `full`.

Use [`../docs/LOCAL_AGENT_MCP_ROUTING_POLICY.md`](../docs/LOCAL_AGENT_MCP_ROUTING_POLICY.md) as the agent instruction that forces raw browser/log/context data through LocalQA before server handoff.

## Architecture

```text
Codex / Claude / Cursor
  -> LocalQA MCP server over stdio
  -> local_agent_run
  -> Playwright browser worker
  -> deterministic checks / browser sessions / extraction
  -> optional local LLM triage or extractive research
  -> compact evidence report for the main LLM
```

The deterministic layer checks:

- page errors
- console errors
- failed network requests
- HTTP 4xx/5xx responses
- horizontal overflow
- clipped interactive elements
- unlabeled controls
- broken images
- missing expected text

The optional local LLM only summarizes and triages evidence. It does not blindly drive the browser.

## MCP tool groups

### Primary delegation tool

- `local_agent_run`
- `localqa_prepare_handoff`

Use `local_agent_run` for normal coding-agent workflows. It routes internally to browser QA, site QA, research, extraction, prompt cleanup, log analysis, handoff gating, and local Bonsai triage.

The `local_agent_run` response explicitly identifies the MCP-local agent boundary:

- `agentType: "local_mcp_agent"`
- `executionMode: "local_first"`
- `publicTool: "local_agent_run"`
- `steps: [...]` (internal tool execution trace)
- `telemetry.internalStepCount`
- `telemetry.externalCalls`
- `enforcement` with runtime guard decisions (`blocked`, `allowedPayload`, `handoffProof`)

### QA tools

- `localqa_health`
- `run_ui_qa`
- `run_site_qa`
- `discover_site_links`
- `read_qa_report`

### Browser session tools

- `browser_start_session`
- `browser_snapshot`
- `browser_act`
- `browser_end_session`
- `browser_list_sessions`

Use these when the coding agent needs a short browser loop: open page, inspect state, click/fill/wait, inspect again.

### Research tools

- `browser_open_page`
- `browser_extract_page`
- `browser_search`
- `browser_research_task`
- `browser_compare_sources`

Use these for coding-related docs/research tasks where the main LLM should receive compact, source-backed snippets instead of raw page dumps.

### Handoff verification guard (host/runtime)

For host-side hard enforcement before any external model/server send:

- call `local_agent_run` with `destinationKind`
- if `enforcement.handoffProof` is present, verify using `localqa_verify_handoff` (available in `agent`/`full` surfaces)
- block send when:
  - `enforcement.blocked=true`
  - or `localqa_verify_handoff.verified=false`

## Safety policy

Default mode is safe-by-default:

- Allowed: read pages, search docs, inspect GitHub/docs, test localhost apps, fill local/test forms, click safe local UI, capture screenshots, extract text.
- Blocked unless explicitly approved: purchases, payments, bookings, job applications, destructive admin actions, account mutations, real-world form submissions, messages/emails.
- `browser_act` blocks risky non-local clicks unless `allowUnsafe=true`.

## CLI usage

Install Playwright if needed:

```bash
npm install -D playwright
npx playwright install chromium
```

Run deterministic QA:

```bash
npm run localqa:run -- \
  --url http://localhost:3000 \
  --goal "Test the signup page for visible UI, console, and form issues"
```

Developer override: run with an optional Ollama summary:

```bash
npm run localqa:run -- \
  --url http://localhost:3000 \
  --goal "Test the signup page" \
  --ollama-model qwen2.5-coder:3b
```

The Ollama path is a developer override only. Initial-release docs, validation, and benchmarks use Bonsai as the single reference model.

Run with Bonsai through the native Prism/llama-server path manually:

```bash
npm run localqa:bonsai:serve
```

In another terminal:

```bash
npm run localqa:run -- \
  --url http://localhost:3000 \
  --goal "Test the signup page for browser, accessibility, layout, console, and network issues" \
  --llm-provider openai-compatible \
  --llm-model bonsai \
  --llm-endpoint http://127.0.0.1:18081/v1/chat/completions \
  --llm-temperature 0.5 \
  --llm-top-k 20 \
  --llm-top-p 0.85 \
  --llm-timeout-ms 60000 \
  --llm-max-tokens 128
```

Smoke-test the MCP server and the Bonsai endpoint together:

```bash
LOCALQA_DEFAULT_LLM=bonsai \
LOCALQA_BONSAI_AUTOSTART=1 \
LOCALQA_LLM_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:18081/v1/chat/completions \
LOCALQA_LLM_MODEL=Bonsai-8B.gguf \
```

For normal MCP client usage, set `LOCALQA_BONSAI_AUTOSTART=1` and the MCP will start the Bonsai server during chat/tool load if it is not already running.

Run scripted interactions before inspection:

```bash
npm run localqa:run -- \
  --url http://localhost:3000/signup \
  --goal "Check signup form behavior" \
  --fill "input[type=email]=test@example.com" \
  --click "button[type=submit]" \
  --wait-for-text "Check your email"
```

Add custom viewports:

```bash
npm run localqa:run -- \
  --url http://localhost:3000 \
  --viewport desktop:1440x900 \
  --viewport mobile:390x844
```

## MCP server

Start the server:

```bash
npm run localqa:mcp
```

Expose this command to a coding agent as an MCP server. The default command uses the official `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` stdio server.

Smoke-test the MCP server locally:

```bash
npm run localqa:mcp:smoke
```

The server provides:

- `local_agent_run`
- `localqa_health`
- `run_ui_qa`
- `read_qa_report`
- `discover_site_links`
- `run_site_qa`
- `browser_start_session`
- `browser_snapshot`
- `browser_act`
- `browser_end_session`
- `browser_extract_page`
- `browser_search`
- `browser_research_task`
- `browser_compare_sources`

`run_ui_qa` returns a compact JSON report with findings, evidence, screenshots, and an approximate token-savings estimate.

`run_site_qa` discovers a bounded same-origin route list or accepts explicit URLs, runs route-level QA, and writes an aggregate `site-report.json`.

The previous newline JSON-RPC server remains available as:

```bash
npm run localqa:mcp:legacy
```

# LocalQA Rules for OpenCode

Use LocalQA as the local evidence and memory layer. The frontier model remains responsible for planning, reasoning, and implementation.

Core rules:

- Before reasoning about raw logs, DOM dumps, browser console output, network traces, stack traces, screenshots, or large tool output, call `local_agent_run`.
- Prefer `filePath` / `filePaths` over pasted raw text when evidence is in local files.
- For complex work, prefer `controlMode: "directed"`: the main agent should specify exact `directedSteps`, budgets, and `outputContract`.
- For sensitive or reproducible work, use `controlMode: "strict"` so unknown local tools are rejected.
- Before repeating prior project investigation, use `controlMode: "memory"` and ask what was already tried, skipped, or proven.
- After meaningful work, use `controlMode: "record"` to write durable local memory with what changed, tests run, result, failures, skipped items, and next steps.
- For browser QA, call `local_agent_run` with `mode: "browser_qa"` or a directed `browser_qa` step instead of manually collecting raw DOM/context into the cloud conversation.
- When a result contains `vault://`, `artifact://`, or `localqa://context-index` handles, use `answer_from_handle` for scoped questions.
- Do not ask for raw vault artifact contents unless the user explicitly approves.
- Do not send raw evidence to an external model/server if LocalQA policy says `rawExternalSendAllowed: false`.
- Treat LocalQA confirmed issues as stronger than suspected/unproven signals.
- If LocalQA reports token savings, preserve those numbers in user-facing summaries.

Directed mode template:

```json
{
  "controlMode": "directed",
  "task": "State the investigation goal.",
  "directedSteps": [
    { "tool": "memory_query", "question": "What did we already try?" },
    { "tool": "context_cleanup", "filePath": "./path/to/evidence.txt", "task": "Extract likely files, commands, risks, and next reads.", "contextBudgetTokens": 1200 }
  ],
  "outputContract": {
    "maxTokens": 1600,
    "include": ["verified_findings", "evidence", "likely_files", "risks", "next_actions"],
    "exclude": ["raw_logs", "raw_dom", "full_file_tree"]
  }
}
```

Privacy boundary:

- These rules do not protect text the user already pasted into the prompt.
- For private logs/files, ask the user for a local path and use LocalQA.
- LocalQA is a context/evidence control layer, not a network-level prompt interceptor.

import { expect, test } from "vitest";

import * as z from "zod/v3";

const beforeBenchmarkDate = new Date(2022, 10, 4);
const benchmarkDate = new Date(2022, 10, 5);
const afterBenchmarkDate = new Date(2022, 10, 6);

const minCheck = z.date().min(benchmarkDate);
const maxCheck = z.date().max(benchmarkDate);

test("passing validations", () => {
  minCheck.parse(benchmarkDate);
  minCheck.parse(afterBenchmarkDate);

  maxCheck.parse(benchmarkDate);
  maxCheck.parse(beforeBenchmarkDate);
});

test("failing validations", () => {
  expect(() => minCheck.parse(beforeBenchmarkDate)).toThrow();
  expect(() => maxCheck.parse(afterBenchmarkDate)).toThrow();
});

test("min max getters", () => {
  expect(minCheck.minDate).toEqual(benchmarkDate);
  expect(minCheck.min(afterBenchmarkDate).minDate).toEqual(afterBenchmarkDate);

  expect(maxCheck.maxDate).toEqual(benchmarkDate);
  expect(maxCheck.max(beforeBenchmarkDate).maxDate).toEqual(beforeBenchmarkDate);
});
